title: The laam of Allah in Al-A'la and our surahs: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 2: Al-A'la, At-Tariq 1 to 8 and waqf
source: Written for quran/y5 lesson 22 (Pupil PDF worksheet: The laam of Allah in Al-A'la and our surahs rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 22. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

keywords.def: the Name Allah: its laam is heavy after fathah or dammah, light after kasrah
the letter ل; its rules decide if it is said, merged, heavy or light

questions.q: Read «ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ» (1:2) and explain the laam.
questions.a: Light: the laam before it has a kasrah (لِ).

questions.q: Heavy or light (pupil PDF): label ten Names of Allah from Al-Fatihah, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Ghashiyah and Al-A'la. Today's rota group recites 87:6 to 10.
questions.a: Answers on the teacher sheet (heavy after fathah or dammah; light after kasrah).

questions.q: Extend: write the rule in your own words.
questions.a: If the letter before Allah has fathah or dammah, the laam is heavy; if kasrah, it is light.

questions.q: Stretch: what happens when we start reciting with the word Allah?
questions.a: We begin with hamzat al-wasl (a fathah), so the laam is heavy.
A) heavy (fathah before). هُوَ ends in a fathah, so the laam of Allah is heavy.

questions.q: After a dammah the laam of Allah is ...
Think again: Why do you think the Name of Allah has its own special rule in tajweed?
questions.a: It is the greatest Name; the Arabs said it with honour, heavy, except after a kasrah where it is light.
